design: plans/cmux-next/chrome-parity/p01-process.md section 2.4 and task p01-process-055. In Chrome's remote_cocoa split the browser process drives RenderWidgetHostViewCocoa in an app shim through RenderWidgetHostNSView and the view answers through RenderWidgetHostNSViewHost. In host mode the Chromium Host is the browser process and cmux's ChromiumHostPageView is the view, so every method of the vendored mojom names its carrier between them. Chrome allows [Sync] calls from the view; cmux has none: what Chrome asks synchronously, the host pushes ahead. scripts/cmux-next/gen-chromium-host-wire.py --check-view-parity checks this file.

targets.event: a CMUX_SHIM_* event kind of cmux_cef_shim.h or an optional event of chromium-host-ops.json
targets.wire: a Kind of Packages/macOS/CmuxNext/ChromiumHost/src/chromium_host_wire.h (page view input and pushed state)

targets.note: how the method maps, when the carrier alone does not say it

A view drawn through a parent ui::Compositor composites inside the host; cmux shows only the CAContexts the host hands it (layer hosting, WIDGET_CONTEXT).

methods.note: Chromium's request to focus the page reaches cmux's focus policy; cmux makes the page view first responder itself (032, 046).

Answers the page window's CAContext id; ChromiumHostPageView hosts it in a CALayerHost (display_ca_layer_tree.mm).
cmux chooses the page background from its theme, fills the page view with it and sends it to the host.
